agentsGuide.title: AI agents setup
agentsGuide.intro: Connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other MCP-capable agents to TMGR. Two MCP servers cover two jobs: working with your tasks, and reaching you when an agent needs attention.
agentsGuide.personaHint: Need an agent to act inside one workspace as a named persona? Create a persona token in Settings → Personas → Connect an agent.

token.heading: 1. Get a token
token.body: Open {link} and press Create token. The token starts with {prefix} and is shown only once, so copy it right away.

connect.heading: 2. Connect your agent
connect.body: Pick your client below. Replace the placeholder with your token. Requires Node 22+ and the TMGR mobile app for pushes and alarms.

taskMcp.heading: Task MCP (tmgr)
taskMcp.body: A remote HTTP MCP server to work with tasks, statuses, comments, time tracking and routines. Generate a device token in {link} and send it in the {header} header.
taskMcp.note: This is not an OAuth connector, so claude.ai custom connectors that require OAuth are not supported.

alarms.heading: Alarms
alarms.body: The {tool} tool rings in the iOS app first, then calls your phone if it is not acknowledged (press 1 to acknowledge). To make it reliable:
alarms.item1: Set and verify an alarm phone in Settings → Agent alerts.
alarms.item2: Add the TMGR caller number to your contacts or Favorites.
alarms.item3: Enable Repeated Calls in iOS settings.
alarms.item4: Allow alarms for the TMGR app.

troubleshooting.heading: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.noPush: No push arrives: check that {path} exists and is readable. Hooks always exit 0 and print nothing.
troubleshooting.mcpList: Run {command} to check the server is connected.
troubleshooting.settingsJson: MCP servers do not go into {file}; use {command}.
troubleshooting.codex: Codex ignores {key} in a project-local {local}; put it in {global}.
troubleshooting.rateLimit: Requests are limited to 20 per minute per token.

plugins.heading: Build a plugin with your agent
plugins.body: Ask your agent to make a TMGR desktop plugin. Point it at {guide} or {llms}: it covers the manifest, permissions and the whole write, test and try loop.
